races.name: Scullion Law 'Law Firm For Life' Ebf Maiden Stakes (gbb Race)
Strathmore Hotels Ltd Novice Stakes (gbb/gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Kissmehoneyhoney
runners_data.note: William Haggas's 4-year-old has strong enough form figures to dominate this field on class (OR 120) and will lead uncontested, though her recent 8-month absence and an 8th-place finish last time out introduce fitness uncertainty; her style fits perfectly for this pace-control scenario, though the STYLE_FIT flag notes a slight role mismatch that warrants mild discount from odds-on faith.

runners_data.name: Tiernan
runners_data.note: Andrew Mullen partners this hold-up operator who has run respectably on Good ground in similar company (three placed efforts from eight Good-going runs) and the 1m3f trip is within his compass, but needing a genuine collapse in pace from an uncontested leader is the fundamental problem with his chance here.

runners_data.name: According To Mark
runners_data.note: PJ McDonald takes the mount for Edward Bethell's consistent placed performer who has finished second three times in recent starts, always at trips of 10-12f on Good ground — the form and profile fit this scenario as the prominent stalker, and the headgear (hood) may sharpen his response when the race develops.

runners_data.name: Sottsfield
runners_data.note: Seb Spencer's lightly raced 3-year-old (only two starts) showed some ability finishing 4th on Good going last time but the 87-day layoff and hold-up style leave him entirely dependent on others doing his work up front, and Dale Swift has limited scope to manufacture momentum from the back in a small field.

runners_data.name: Midnight Serenade
runners_data.note: A debut runner for R Mike Smith with the tongue-tie flag and an amateur claimer aboard — an entirely unknown quantity whose OR of 120 appears notional, and with no racecourse form the going and trip suitability cannot be assessed; represents the maximum uncertainty element of this field.

races.paceDynamic: Kissmehoneyhoney is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this five-runner field and, with no credible challenger for the lead, she will dictate terms at whatever tempo suits William Haggas's stable — almost certainly a measured, honest gallop around Hamilton's undulating 1m3f track. According To Mark is the other prominent-style runner but is unlikely to contest the front, meaning the pace will be uncontested and the sectionals will not be punishing. Tiernan and Sottsfield are both hold-up types who will need the pace to truly collapse in front of them to mount a late challenge, but a solo leader controlling tempo rarely generates that scenario. This race shape strongly favours a prominent-to-lead profile: a horse who can track Kissmehoneyhoney closely, or at least race in her slipstream, will be best placed when the race quickens in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Kissmehoneyhoney sets an uncontested, sustainable gallop and the hold-up horses are left with too much to do from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Kissmehoneyhoney dictates every fraction unchallenged and, with Hamilton's demanding finish suiting a horse already in rhythm, she simply outstays all rivals; According To Mark, racing close behind, is the main threat to peg her back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If According To Mark tracks Kissmehoneyhoney closely throughout and quickens past her inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Haggas's mare sets a sufficient pace for According To Mark to have cover and momentum in behind, and PJ McDonald times the move to capitalise on any late fade; According To Mark's consistent placed form at this trip and going profile makes this the most credible alternative outcome.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally faster than expected and Kissmehoneyhoney ties up late, allowing the closers to reel her in.
scenarios.body: Tiernan has the most relevant form credentials among the hold-up runners, with multiple placed efforts on Good going and over this kind of trip, and Andrew Mullen could thread through late; Sottsfield is the wildcard hold-up type but has only two starts and lacks the experience to make this count reliably.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debutant Causes Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Midnight Serenade, a lightly raced unknown with headgear noted, produces an unexpectedly high ceiling on debut.
scenarios.body: A complete unknown quantity with no racecourse form makes meaningful probability assessment impossible, but the tongue-tie flag and amateur jockey booking (Amie Waugh, 3lb claimer) introduce variance; she would need a vastly superior rating ceiling than currently demonstrated to feature.

watchPoints.text: Kissmehoneyhoney's 92-day absence combined with her below-par final run last season means fitness is not guaranteed — watch whether she shows her usual fluent stride in the opening quarter-mile or looks laboured early.

According To Mark has finished second in three of four recent starts and has the profile to exploit any weakness from Kissmehoneyhoney late — watch how tightly PJ McDonald positions him in the first half of the race, as cover early could translate into a decisive move.

Midnight Serenade's debut with tongue-tie and a 3lb claimer aboard introduces behavioural uncertainty — watch for any pre-race market moves or erratic early positioning that could disrupt the otherwise clean pace structure.

Hamilton's finishing straight is testing and genuinely punishes horses that have burned energy fighting for position — the small field size here means Tiernan and Sottsfield will need to be threading through traffic late, which is a near non-issue, but they still need a true gallop to close the gap.

With only five runners and no pace controversy, the race is unlikely to produce unusual sectionals — any significant drifting in the betting ring on Kissmehoneyhoney should be treated as a meaningful fitness signal given her layoff.

races.name: Pdm Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Cabrera
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner whose STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) signals he is marginally racing out of his most comfortable role, but with no rivals to pressure him he should find things easier at the head of affairs; Good going is fine, 15 days since last run looks sharp enough, and five starts at 12f suggest the 1m5f trip is a slight question mark.
runners_data.comment: Cabrera heads this 11-runner field on our ratings and arrives on a quick 15-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going. Winless in her last five starts, a fourth four starts back hints at consistency, and she looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: High Point
runners_data.note: Returned to form with a soft-ground win over 12f last time and has placed credentials at 16f on Standard — the step back to Good ground at Hamilton is the key test; natural hold-up style should see him positioned last or near-last, meaning he needs the pace to truly stack up in the straight.
runners_data.comment: High Point arrives on the back of a win last time and a third three starts back, with experience of today's trip and going working in his favour — the main concern is the 51-day absence since that victory.

runners_data.name: Secret Force
runners_data.note: Strong profile for this race — three wins on Good ground, multiple wins at 17-18f, and a prominent racing style that maps perfectly onto the expected shape; trainer Keatley has four winners from 19 runners in 14 days, adding confidence that the horse arrives fit and ready.
runners_data.comment: Secret Force won two starts back and has gone over today's going before, but he was seventh last time out and his speed rating lags behind his official mark — a profile that places him squarely in the middle of this field.

runners_data.name: Gentle Warrior
runners_data.note: Headgear listed (hood/p), which is worth noting; wears down rivals from the rear and has placed twice on Good ground at 13-14f, but the step to 1m5f and a slow-tempo scenario could leave him with too much to do in what is likely a well-strung-out field.
runners_data.comment: Shaped with promise when second a few starts back and ran respectably in fourth next time, Gentle Warrior has run over today's trip and going and steps forward on an eye-catching rating — the main concern is he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Dunkeld Dreamer
runners_data.note: Progressive three-year-old with four wins in current form cycle, all on Good ground and over increasing trips; prominent racing style ideally suits a pace scenario where he can track Cabrera and kick on — very strong fit with the dominant race shape here.
runners_data.comment: Dunkeld Dreamer showed a sharp turn of foot to win two starts back, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions working in her favour — the worry is whether she can bounce back from a fourth last time out.

runners_data.name: Ouro Preto
runners_data.note: Consistent course form at Hamilton is the headline here — naturally a hold-up horse who has been mapped to midfield given the congestion at the rear; six consecutive finishes outside the placings on similar going suggest limited upside even if he does get a more favourable position than usual.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with unplaced efforts dominating his recent form, Ouro Preto cuts a difficult figure from our ninth-ranked position in the field; he has run over today's trip and going before, but little in his profile suggests a dramatic turnaround here.

runners_data.name: Eroico
runners_data.note: Has placed on Good ground and at similar trips, showing he stays well, but a natural hold-up style means he relies on a genuinely strong gallop to close; the redistribution into midfield does not reflect how this horse actually races, and a controlled Cabrera-led tempo would leave him with too much ground to make up.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Eroico returns after 38 days off carrying 129 lb, and a second four starts back hints at better, though a ninth two starts back and fourth last time out are harder to ignore.

runners_data.name: Spanish Hustle
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old whose recent form figures (8-0066) are poor, and the Going Preferred flag (p) suggests he is best on faster ground than Good; hold-up style and declining form make this a tough ask even in a well-run race.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with back-to-back sixth-place finishes following a pair of unplaced efforts, Spanish Hustle carries 129 lb for a trainer in a lean spell (2/37 over 14 days), though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns after a fair 21-day break.

runners_data.name: Gallus Norman
runners_data.note: Raced just 1 day ago which is an immediate red flag for recovery, though the trainer Goldie runs horses quickly when they are in form; natural closer whose hold-up style is his genuine modus operandi — best chance if the pace is strong enough to bring him into play, but recency of the run is a serious concern.
runners_data.comment: Beaten in his last start and running again just a day later, Gallus Norman faces a stiff task from a yard that has managed just 2 wins from 37 runners in the last fortnight; experience over today's trip and going is a mild plus, but he ranks tenth of eleven on our figures.

runners_data.name: Cotton Bud
runners_data.note: 79 days off the track is a question mark, and the mare's best form has come over shorter trips (10f win, places at 8f); prominent style suits the expected race shape, but the fitness concern and step up in trip make this a speculative runner.
runners_data.comment: Cotton Bud won two starts back and was second three starts back, showing she has the ability, but a sixth last time out and 79 days off cloud her claims; she has experience on today's going, though her speed rating leaves a little to prove.

runners_data.name: Wootton's Gal
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced three-year-old with only three starts to her name — placed twice on Good ground but over shorter trips (11-12f); a true rear-runner who sits in midfield on this map purely because of congestion, meaning she is unlikely to get an ideal position and faces a significant trip test at 1m5f.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked bottom of our figures, Wootton's Gal faces a stiff ask, with a struggling trainer (1/45 in the past fortnight) adding to concerns; second two starts back is the sole encouragement, and she has run over today's going.

races.paceDynamic: Cabrera is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 1m5f Hamilton handicap and, with no genuine rival likely to dispute the lead, should be able to control the tempo from the outset at a pace of his own choosing. Dunkeld Dreamer and Secret Force are the likeliest horses to track him from a prominent position, creating a small, organised lead group while the bulk of the field strings out behind. The redistribution flag is important here: Ouro Preto, Eroico, Gallus Norman and Wootton's Gal are all true hold-up types who have been mapped forward because the field contains more rear-rank horses than the race shape can accommodate at the back — in a comfortable, Cabrera-controlled gallop, those horses are unlikely to find themselves in their natural position and cannot rely on a muddling, collapsing pace to bring them into play. This race shape — a lone leader setting an honest but manageable gallop over a stamina-testing 1m5f on good ground — unambiguously favours prominent racers with the fitness and class to track the pace and pick up in the straight, rewarding horses like Secret Force and Dunkeld Dreamer over genuine hold-up types who need chaos to close the gap.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cabrera Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Cabrera leads unchallenged at a steady-to-honest gallop and the race develops into a test of sustained stamina from the front.
scenarios.body: Cabrera sets the fractions alone, the prominent duo of Secret Force and Dunkeld Dreamer travel within themselves tracking him, and one or both overhaul him in the long Hamilton straight; Good ground and a fair pace reward the horse with the best cruising speed and class at this distance.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Outstays Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Cabrera goes slightly quicker than expected and tows the race along at a gallop that tests stamina more severely, setting it up for the best stayer tracking him.
scenarios.body: A sustained pace over 1m5f on Good ground plays into the hands of a genuine stayer who has been travelling comfortably in second or third, kicking clear when Cabrera weakens in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final quarter-mile after Cabrera has been pressured or the gallop is genuinely strong enough to bring closers into contention.
scenarios.body: A strong pace that burns off the front-running threat allows a genuine stayer from further back to pick up strongly late; Gallus Norman and High Point are the most credible candidates from this group if they can find a clear passage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Cabrera is able to control the race at an unusually slow tempo such that nothing behind him can pick up and he steals it from the front.
scenarios.body: A falsely run race over this stamina trip suits a front-runner who conserves energy and sprints for home; this scenario is unlikely given the prominence of Dunkeld Dreamer and Secret Force who will not allow a complete dawdle.

watchPoints.text: Gallus Norman ran just 1 day ago — monitor closely in the paddock and early in the race for any signs of fatigue or reluctance that would confirm the quick turnaround is too sharp.
Secret Force is the standout prominent profile fit but represents Irish-trained raider territory — watch for any market drift in the final minutes that might indicate a stable confidence issue.

Ouro Preto, Eroico and Wootton's Gal are genuine hold-up types likely to find themselves further forward than ideal given the field composition — if any of them push for a prominent berth early, it could unbalance their race entirely.

Cotton Bud's 79-day absence warrants watching in the pre-race ring; if she shows any signs of ring-rustiness or is unfurnished in condition, her prominent style becomes less of an asset despite suiting the pace shape.

Cabrera's jockey P J McDonald is a quality booking that elevates confidence in a controlled front-running display — watch whether he goes straight to the front or tries to restrain, as that will define the entire race tempo within the first furlong.

races.name: Cube Glass 'soba' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Corolla Point
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner stepping back up after two recent placed efforts on Good and Soft 5f; PJ McDonald takes over and Edward Bethell's yard is 2/25 in the last 14 days — solid conditions but the prominent tag here means it's racing in its natural lead role, and the STYLE_FIT score reflects it can be discounted if it fails to secure the front.
runners_data.comment: Corolla Point arrives with a consistent recent profile — placed three times and a winner twice in his last five starts, with experience of today's trip and going. He carries 140 lb from stall 11, and whether that weight can be conceded all round is the key question.

runners_data.name: Purosangue
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for Robert Cowell with zero wins or places from 15 similar-going runs — a deeply uninspiring Good-ground profile and the widest-drawn, deepest-held horse in the race; Kaiya Fraser rides but the overall evidence gives little encouragement at these conditions.
runners_data.comment: Mostly finishing in mid-division in recent starts, Purosangue has run over today's trip and going, and his rating of 106 puts him narrowly clear at the top of these 14; yet to win in his last five, he needs to convert that solid placing form into something more decisive.

runners_data.name: Arklow Lad
runners_data.note: Conor Whiteley (5lb claim) on a horse showing a lively recent form string of 13151 — three wins from five runs including back-to-back 5f victories; the tongue-piece is worn and Michael Appleby's yard fired a winner 1/28 in the last 14 days, making this a lively each-way contender from a prominent pitch.
runners_data.comment: Arklow Lad brings solid recent form — a winner last time out and a winner three starts back, with experience over today's trip and going — but 56 days off the track and a trainer firing at just 4% in the last fortnight are real concerns for this 135 lb burden.

runners_data.name: Another Baar
runners_data.note: Headgear (tongue-tie) in use and recent form reads 100060 — nothing there to inspire confidence; only 4 wins and 5 places from 15 similar-going attempts, Adrian Keatley's raider looks to need things to fall very kindly.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to win one start back but has been out of the frame in his last two, and that patchy recent profile is hard to ignore; has run over today's trip and going, though, and 36 days between runs leaves him with something to prove on return.

runners_data.name: Manila Scouse
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who has been running consistently on Good ground with 2W4P from 15 similar-going efforts — the best Good-ground profile in the field; Tim Easterby's yard is in excellent 14-day form (6/88) and Sean Kirrane takes the ride on a horse that genuinely handles this surface and distance combination.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 12 of 14 on our figures, Manila Scouse is hard to fancy despite winning last time out — that sole success in his last five starts is offset by some inconsistent efforts either side of it. Has run over today's distance and going, and 26 days between runs shouldn't inconvenience him.

runners_data.name: Eternal Sunshine
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's six-year-old ran just 7 days ago — the quick turnaround is a flag — and while it is a naturally prominent racer, the congestion of pace types in this field means it is highly unlikely to secure its preferred position; STYLE_FIT discount applies and the 16th-place finish last time on Good over 6f is not encouraging.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts with two unplaced efforts sandwiching modest efforts at best, Eternal Sunshine heads here just seven days after her latest outing — a quick turnaround for a mare ranked 13th of 14 on our figures, and with her trainer in poor recent form at 5%.

runners_data.name: Venture Capital
runners_data.note: 108 days off the track is a significant concern for Kevin Ryan's five-year-old; a true hold-up horse shuffled into a midfield mapping due to the distribution of the field, its best result on Good ground was a third from 9 similar-going efforts, and the lack of recent evidence makes this a risky proposition.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with an eighth last time out after 108 days off the track, Venture Capital does have experience over today's distance and going — but a trainer without a win in 22 recent attempts and a third five starts back are limited positives to cling to.

runners_data.name: Fivethousandtoone
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old veteran whose natural instinct is to race prominently, though the overcrowded pace map means it is likely to find itself further back than it wants to be; the 0W0P from 15 similar-going runs is damning for a horse that has been around long enough to show something, and Tim Easterby's stable runner looks more likely to be a foil.
runners_data.comment: Fivethousandtoone has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 103 ranks him second of 14 — a strong profile despite being winless in recent starts; the risk is that his last three runs show a slide in form.

runners_data.name: Parisiac
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's seven-year-old won a 5f Good-ground race two runs ago (form 1220 recently) and is a confirmed prominent racer who will want to be up with the pace — but with multiple rivals chasing the same slots, it is very likely to get pushed further back than suits; the STYLE_FIT discount is meaningful here despite the decent recent form.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Parisiac is hard to fancy despite the distance and going experience; a winner four starts back, he has been unplaced on his most recent outing and faces a stiff task from stall one carrying 122 lb.

runners_data.name: Solar Aclaim
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's five-year-old holds a 5f win on Soft ground but its Good-going record is very thin (3/15) with no wins or places; Sam James takes the ride but the recent form of 00819 is worrying and the hold-up style means it depends entirely on a pace collapse.
runners_data.comment: Solar Acclaim showed he can win at this level with a victory two starts back, but a ninth last time out raises questions about consistency; he has run over today's trip and going, and his 134 lb burden won't help him recapture that form.

runners_data.name: Fluorescence
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell four-year-old with a recent pulled-up run (U) in the form string — that question mark must be answered; 2W3P from 10 similar-going runs shows some competence on Good turf and Gina Mangan accepts the ride, but the erratic form makes this a risky prominent-type selection at a competitive OR of 90.
runners_data.comment: Fluorescence has run over today's trip and going, and her two fourths in recent starts show she's capable of mixing it at this level — the unseated rider blot aside, her profile makes her a genuine danger here; the concern is she remains winless in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Vantheman
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's five-year-old carries the blinkers for the first time and boasts 1W3P from 10 similar-going runs including a course win at 5f Good — the track-and-going profile is one of the strongest here; Tom Eaves rides and a 15-day gap between runs suggests freshness; the prominent style suits this race shape well.
runners_data.comment: Vantheman was third three starts back and has run over today's trip and going, but consecutive fourths in his last two outings and a trainer without a winner in 22 recent attempts are real concerns alongside 130 lb to carry.

runners_data.name: Jordan Electrics
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old veteran for Jim Goldie who is actually in strong form (954831) with a recent 6f Good win and Paul Mulrennan in the saddle — the hold-up style is genuine and the Good-going profile is solid (1W3P from 11 runs); at OR 86 and dropping back in class sense, this is a credible late challenger.
runners_data.comment: Winner last time out and has run over today's trip and going, but his record in recent starts has been inconsistent and he heads here with a trainer firing at just 5% over the past fortnight — grounds for optimism and caution in equal measure.

runners_data.name: Canon's House
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby five-year-old with the yard in decent 3/32 form over the last fortnight; Mark Winn takes the ride on a horse with 2W2P from 6 similar-going runs and a prominent style that should see it competitive — the 27-day absence is within normal range and it has shown course aptitude.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 11th of 14 on our figures, Canon's House faces a stiff ask from stall 12 carrying 128 lb, though he has run over today's distance and going before, and a third last time out at least hints at residual ability.

races.paceDynamic: Corolla Point is the one confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner field and, with no genuine pace rival likely to press hard from the outset, should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over Hamilton's flat 5f. Manila Scouse, Arklow Lad, Vantheman and Fluorescence all carry prominent styles and will be angling for a position close to the pace, creating a competitive early shuffle for front-rank berths but not a true burn-up. The field contains more natural front-running and prominent types than the map can accommodate — Eternal Sunshine, Fivethousandtoone and Parisiac are genuine prominent racers but are realistically going to find themselves in a midfield slot against their nature, reducing their likely effectiveness. With a single pace-setter setting a measured tempo and several hold-up horses carrying redistributed tags that undermine their late-kick credentials, this race shape strongly favours horses that can sit a length or two off the lead without covering excess ground — genuine prominent-to-midfield closers with the ability to pick off a controlled leader in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Corolla Point Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Corolla Point secures the lead uncontested and sets a true-to-form sustainable gallop, allowing it to control sectionals throughout.
scenarios.body: Corolla Point rolls to the front without a serious fight and, running from its natural pace-setting role on Good ground it handles, has every chance to keep rivals honest without emptying the tank early; the flat 5f at Hamilton suits a horse that can dictate and not get headed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely steady and the horses sitting close behind Corolla Point produce a decisive late challenge in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Manila Scouse, Arklow Lad and Vantheman all track the leader in their natural position and, as the field compresses entering the final 1f, any one of this trio can produce a sharp enough effort to collar the leader on Good turf they have each handled before; Vantheman and Jordan Electrics have both shown strong finishing form over course-and-distance type conditions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves faster than expected through the first 2f and the front-runners tie up, allowing hold-up runners to benefit from a pace collapse late.
scenarios.body: Jordan Electrics and Solar Aclaim sit deepest and would be the primary beneficiaries if early fractions are quicker than anticipated and the field strings out, creating room to sprint through gaps; Solar Aclaim has a win at 5f on Soft going in its recent history but its Good-going profile is limited, making this a conditional scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Heats Up, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types refuse to concede position at the start and a competitive early dash burns out the front rank before halfway.
scenarios.body: With Eternal Sunshine, Fivethousandtoone and Parisiac all naturally wanting to race prominently, an unusually fierce early battle could materialise despite predictions, compromising Corolla Point's control and leaving the race wide open late; this is the least likely shape given the clear pace hierarchy but a big field over 5f always carries this risk.

watchPoints.text: Arklow Lad — three wins from his last five starts including two at 5f, strong claimer aboard and a tongue-piece applied; if he jumps well and slots just behind Corolla Point he becomes a serious winning threat.

Vantheman — course winner over 5f on Good ground wearing blinkers for the first time, which often triggers a sharp uptick in effort; Tom Eaves knows the horse and this combination of fresh headgear and track-specific form is the key danger to the likely front-runner.

Corolla Point — its ability to get a clean lead is not guaranteed with Manila Scouse and Arklow Lad both pressing for the same prominent berths; if it is headed early and forced to race off an honest gallop rather than dictating, its chance is meaningfully compromised.

Eternal Sunshine and Fivethousandtoone — both are natural prominent racers who are realistically going to be shuffled back against their will in this field; monitor their early behaviour in the stalls and first few strides, as a poor break from either locks them into an unsuitable position throughout.

Manila Scouse — the best raw Good-ground profile in this race (12/15 runs, 2W4P) and Tim Easterby's yard is firing at 6/88 over 14 days; the seven-year-old is quietly consistent and could easily outrun a bigger price if Corolla Point sets an honest but not punishing tempo.

races.name: Blitz Cleaning Commercial Cleaning Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Hundred Caps
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's 4yo has solid Good-ground form and races from a prominent position; she is the lone confirmed front-runner here and sets the tactical agenda, though her recent form figures of 225574 suggest she is vulnerable to being run down late once headed.
runners_data.comment: Hundred Caps has shown consistent placing ability with two seconds in recent starts, and has experience of today's trip and conditions — though he's yet to score in his last six outings, our rating of 83, top of these, makes him the one to side with here.

runners_data.name: Stirrup Cup
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's hold-up 4yo has a 45-day break to factor in, has run well on Good ground at 6f but steps back to 5f where his two best efforts came; he needs the pace to collapse to get involved.
runners_data.comment: Stirrup Cup landed a win two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, giving him every chance to fire fresh after 45 days off; the fifth last time out is the one to forgive.

runners_data.name: Tiriac
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's 6yo hold-up type has a poor recent form string of 97805 and no wins or placed efforts from similar going in recent runs; hard to see where the improvement comes from at OR 71.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Tiriac nonetheless catches the eye on a our rating of 80 — nine pounds clear of his official mark — and has experience of today's trip and going; the concern is that his recent finishes offer little encouragement.

runners_data.name: King's Crown
runners_data.note: Michael Dods's consistent if frustrating 6yo has placed at this trip on Good ground but the form reads 665340 — frequently thereabouts without winning; hold-up style means he needs something to go wrong for the prominent horses.
runners_data.comment: King's Crown showed clear promise when third three starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going is a solid foundation; the concern is that he has been winless in his last six starts, with an unplaced effort last time requiring a bounce-back.

runners_data.name: Harb
runners_data.note: Tristan Davidson's 7yo is a genuine hold-up horse by nature but the field's density of closers means he is unlikely to find his preferred berth at the rear; recent run at 7d ago is sharp, and his last win came over this exact trip on Good going, so stamina is not the concern — positioning is.
runners_data.comment: Harb showed a third two starts back but has since disappointed, and his sole win in recent starts came five starts back; he has run over today's trip and going, though 122 lb from stall 9 gives him plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Thunderstorm Katie
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's 5yo was racing just one day ago which is an unusually tight turnaround and must be a flag; she is a true closer who has placed five times in her last five runs on Good ground but is mapped into a midfield slot she would not naturally occupy given the field's hold-up traffic jam.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts despite four runner-up finishes, Thunderstorm Katie ran just yesterday and faces a stiff ask ranked last on our figures; her trainer is badly out of form, though she does have experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Mount Ruapehu
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's 6yo is a prominent type whose form reads 886664 — running into places without threatening; he should press Hundred Caps early but his flat form curve makes him more of a pace facilitator than a winner here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with three sixths and two eighths among those recent figures, Mount Ruapehu faces an uphill task ranked 11 of 12 on our ratings; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 12 days between runs suggests he's at least fresh.

runners_data.name: Never Dark
runners_data.note: A 9yo hold-up specialist for Iain Jardine whose natural finishing position gets crowded out when this many closers contest the same race; recent form of 387-66 is uninspiring and the step back to 5f from preferred 6f settings is a further query.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Never Dark's sole encouragement is a third five starts back, though a sequence of mid-to-rear finishes since then and a rating of 58 make it hard to fancy him turning things around from stall 10.

runners_data.name: Little Mi Mi
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's 5yo prominent racer has won over this trip and on this type of ground, with a form figure of 1 at 5f on Good; Andrew Mullen takes the ride and the horse's ability to press the pace while still finding plenty late makes it a key player in most scenarios.
runners_data.comment: Winner last time out, she has shown she can find the line — but that unplaced effort three starts back tempers confidence, and carrying 130 lb from stall 4 adds to the task, even with experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Oriental Prince
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's 5yo hold-up runner has a form string of 050748 and has not placed on Good ground in recent runs; ridden by Paul Mulrennan but the raw numbers do not make a compelling case at OR 69 against these rivals.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last six starts, and trainer's current 5% strike rate over 14 days offers little encouragement; however, Oriental Prince has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating edges above his official mark of 69, hinting at residual ability.

runners_data.name: Iris Dancer
runners_data.note: Tristan Davidson's 8yo prominent mare is in excellent current form — wins at 1/6f and 1/6f in recent outings on Good ground — and Kaiya Fraser rides; the step back to 5f from 6f is a slight query but the consistent place record and Good-ground affinity mark her as a major player if she can travel close to the pace.
runners_data.comment: Iris Dancer shaped well with a third last time out, and a winner two starts back, but ranked tenth of twelve on our figures she faces a stiff ask here; experience over today's trip and going at least counts in her favour.

runners_data.name: Jm Jhingree
runners_data.note: Ewan Whillans's 4yo is a genuine hold-up runner who won over this exact trip on Good ground in his last-but-two start; Greg Fairley rides, and he has the tactical profile to finish off a truly-run race, but is shuffled into a midfield slot that dilutes his ability to produce his best closing run in a field this congested with hold-up types.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten two runs ago since winning three starts back, Jm Jhingree is ranked ninth of twelve on our figures and has plenty to prove at 126 lb from stall eight, though he has run over today's trip and going before and bounced back with a third last time out.

races.paceDynamic: Hundred Caps is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 5f sprint on Good ground at Hamilton, and with no credible challenger for the lead, she is set to stride clear from the gates and control tempo at a manageable, self-chosen pace rather than being dragged into a war. Mount Ruapehu and Little Mi Mi will press forward from prominent positions to track her, meaning the pace should be honest but not frantic — a sustainable gallop that keeps the race honest without burning off those who travel close to the speed. The field contains a surplus of hold-up types — Jm Jhingree, Harb, Thunderstorm Katie, and Never Dark are all genuine rear-division horses who cannot all find their natural berth and have been mapped into midfield as a consequence, meaning the race shape will be more compressed than the labels suggest. This race favours horses who can race prominently, travel smoothly in the slipstream of Hundred Caps, and produce a sustained finish rather than a true late sprint — prominent and pace-pressing profiles are best suited.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hundred Caps Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Hundred Caps secures the lead unchallenged and sets a true but not suicidal pace, allowing her to dominate from the front.
scenarios.body: Hundred Caps dictates on her own terms with Mount Ruapehu and Little Mi Mi as the nearest threats in her wake, but with no one willing to pressure her early the race becomes a procession for those who travelled prominently throughout. Horses who track the leader through the first two furlongs and maintain their position into the straight are the clear beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Hundred Caps sets a pace that strings the field out and Little Mi Mi or Iris Dancer track her efficiently before asserting approaching the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The honest but uncontested tempo allows the prominent trackers to conserve enough energy to pick off the leader inside the final furlong as the shorter-priced runners carry more weight into the closing stages. Little Mi Mi's course and distance form and Iris Dancer's consistent recent profile — both winners over Good ground — make them prime candidates in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply early and the front-runners tie each other up, creating a compressed final-furlong dash that rewards a strong finisher.
scenarios.body: Thunderstorm Katie's relentless top-two finishes on this ground profile and Jm Jhingree's recent win over this exact course and distance mark them as the most plausible late challengers, though both are mapped into midfield rather than their natural rear position, limiting the scope of any late burst. This scenario is discounted because the true hold-up horses cannot all get back far enough to generate the momentum a genuine late swoop requires.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Hundred Caps is taken on early by Mount Ruapehu or another horse breaking sharply, causing a faster-than-expected gallop that burns all the prominent runners out.
scenarios.body: Stirrup Cup and King's Crown, who have shown the ability to finish off races from off the pace at this sort of trip, could theoretically collect the pieces, but neither has the recent form or course figures to inspire confidence in this shape. This is the least likely scenario given the absence of a genuine pace challenger and the compressed nature of the mid-pack.

watchPoints.text: Hundred Caps holds the key to the race shape — if she bounces straight to the front unchallenged and is allowed to dictate at a comfortable tempo, she becomes very difficult to peg back at this trip over 5f on Good ground.

Thunderstorm Katie ran just one day ago and her turnaround time should be monitored in the parade ring for any signs of fatigue or stress; a horse in peak condition could be a value play but the timing is unusually sharp.

Little Mi Mi and Iris Dancer are both prominent types whose ability to press Hundred Caps while still finding a finish makes them dangerous — watch whether they travel together in the first two furlongs or one drops off the pace early, which would change the shape significantly.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — Jm Jhingree, Harb, Thunderstorm Katie, Never Dark — will not all find space to settle at the rear; watch the early positioning in the first furlong to see which of them actually drops away and which is forced to race closer than ideal.

Iain Jardine saddles three runners (Mount Ruapehu, Never Dark, Little Mi Mi) and stable tactics may influence which horse is given a positive ride — Little Mi Mi appears the stable's strongest candidate on form but inter-stable dynamics are worth tracking in the market before the off.

races.name: Gss Contracts Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Rajapour
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 8f on Good and has four places from nine runs on similar going, making him one of the better-credentialed horses in the field for today's conditions; a natural hold-up horse who will need to find a clear run from the rear, which is the primary concern given the compressed midfield pack, but his David O'Meara stable is firing at 5/50 over 14 days and he carries top-priced headgear (tp).
runners_data.comment: Rajapour has winning form two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, so conditions hold no fears; he's fit on a seven-day turnaround and our rating puts him firmly in contention, though the fall last time is the one note of caution.

runners_data.name: Intrusively
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's four-year-old has placed four times on Good going and ran three consecutive 4th-place finishes on similar ground, suggesting consistency without a winning punch; natural hold-up style means he is reliant on a strong pace he is unlikely to get today, and 23 days between runs is unremarkable, though his weight of 142lbs is the second heaviest in the field.
runners_data.comment: Intrusively has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating of 89 puts him clear at the head of the rankings; he returns after 23 days in good order from stall two carrying 142 lb. Winless in his last six starts, though three consecutive fourths hint at consistency, and a trainer in poor current form is the one note of caution.

runners_data.name: Sunriseontheboyne
runners_data.note: Ben Haslam's gelding drops back having shown little in recent outings on Standard surfaces, with only one win and three places from 15 similar-going starts; a hold-up operator returning after 60 days off, that significant layoff combined with the weakest recent form record in the field makes his reappearance fitness a legitimate query, and his best historical results have come at shorter distances.
runners_data.comment: Sunriseontheboyne has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 78 gives him a case as a leading threat off 140 lb from stall 7 — though he's winless in his last six starts, and that persistent inability to convert remains the clear concern.

runners_data.name: Mwafaq
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey's four-year-old arrives with the most compelling recent form in the race — three wins in the last five, including back-to-back victories on Good ground, and he wears a hood (p) to maintain concentration; a natural prominent racer, he is best placed to exploit the solo front-runner by sitting on Sanafi Zabeel's quarters and making a sustained challenge in the straight, and his apprentice rider Ethan Tindall (5lb claimer) could offset the higher weight.
runners_data.comment: Mwafaq arrives in decent nick — a winner two starts back and scored last time out — and has run over today's trip and going before, but carrying 138 lb from stall 9 for a trainer striking at just 2% recently makes him hard to fancy, ranked eighth on our figures.

runners_data.name: Midsummer Storm
runners_data.note: K. R. Burke sends this three-year-old in reasonable form — a 3rd and 4th from four career runs — with the stable hitting 8/36 over 14 days; he is a genuine hold-up type by nature but the crowded rear means he will likely race closer to the pace than ideal, and having only two runs on Good ground with no wins or places on that surface, there are more questions than answers here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, with a sixth last time out and his best recent effort a third three starts back, Midsummer Storm faces a stiff task from the bottom of the ratings; experience over today's trip and going at least counts for something.

runners_data.name: Sanafi Zabeel
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's five-year-old is the pivotal horse in this race as the lone confirmed front-runner; five of six recent runs have come on Good ground with a win and four places, and he clearly handles this surface, making his ability to control fractions from the front unchallenged a major tactical asset for Mulrennan — the critical question is whether he has enough in reserve to hold on over this 1m½f trip.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and carrying a hefty 132 lb, Sanafi Zabeel is hard to fancy despite back-to-back thirds showing some consistency; a struggling trainer at 2/37 in the last 14 days does him no favours either, though he has distance and going experience and returns on a reasonable 16-day break.

runners_data.name: Watcha Snoop
runners_data.note: Adam Nicol's three-year-old carries a ⚠ fading-in-finish flag and has never placed higher than 10th in recent form, with a string of double-figure finishes across Good and Standard surfaces; a true hold-up horse pushed into a midfield map position by sheer field composition, the fade tendency combined with raw form figures makes this one of the more difficult profiles to advocate for regardless of race shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and drawn in stall one carrying 132 lb, Watcha Snoop at least has experience of today's going, and a speed rating of 78 offers a sliver of encouragement — though he'll need a marked upturn in form to get involved here.

runners_data.name: Starliner
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt's five-year-old has been consistent on Good ground — two 2nd-place finishes from her last three starts on Good, all at 8f — and wears a hood (p) to maintain focus; by nature a hold-up operator, she will be racing further forward than ideal given the redistribution, but her proven form on this going at this trip range gives her a better claim than several others in the same position, and the Perratt stable is active at 4/9 over 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Twice placed in his last two starts, Starliner arrives in decent nick just 12 days since his most recent outing, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; yet winless in his last six, the 130 lb burden from stall 6 makes a step up to winning all the harder.

runners_data.name: Ephron
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's three-year-old has a win on Good ground over 8f and a 2nd on Soft, showing he handles genuine turf, though his most recent run was a 7th over 10f on Good; a hold-up horse operating out of his preferred rear position due to field composition, the step back from 10f to 1m½f is worth noting as potentially better suiting his profile, and Conor Whiteley's 5lb claim softens the burden.
runners_data.comment: Ephron's runner-up finish two starts back underlines his claims here, and he has experience over today's trip and going; the risk is that seventh on his latest start leaves something to prove on current form.

runners_data.name: Yaaser
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's eight-year-old veteran has seven wins on his record but recent form shows only a 3rd from his last 15 Good-going runs — a thin return — and his form string of 975953 lacks conviction; at OR 58, the lowest in the field, he is well-weighted by concession from rivals, but a horse pushed into midfield from his natural hold-up berth, with no win at this distance and a moderate strike rate on this going, faces a stiff ask.
runners_data.comment: Yaaser ran third last time out — his best recent effort — but has been winless in his last six starts and his trainer is in poor form at just 5% over the past fortnight; he has run over today's trip and going before, though his official rating of 58 is a concern.

races.paceDynamic: Sanafi Zabeel is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to pressurise him, Paul Mulrennan can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this mile-and-a-half at Hamilton. His recent form on Good going is solid — five of his last six runs have come on similar ground — and his natural tendency to bowl along in front without being harried makes him a significant tactical factor. The remainder of the field is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up types who will track midfield or worse, meaning the race is likely to develop as a steady-pace procession with Sanafi Zabeel controlling fractions and the closers burning ground on a long run to the line. This shape firmly favours prominent or patient closers who can sit just behind the pace and pounce in the final two furlongs rather than deep hold-up horses needing a strong pace injection that simply will not materialise. The field holds materially more hold-up horses than can realistically operate at the rear — Midsummer Storm, Watcha Snoop, Starliner, Ephron, and Yaaser are all mapped forward of their natural position, meaning the true contention for prominent early spots behind Sanafi Zabeel is fiercer than the map suggests, with Mwafaq and Rajapour most likely to actually secure those positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sanafi Zabeel Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Sanafi Zabeel bowls clear from the gates and no rival has the early pace or intent to go with him, setting a comfortable solo lead.
scenarios.body: Mulrennan dictates every fraction and the field trails in a compressed, slow-burn group, meaning those nearest the leader get the best run to the line while true deep closers get no pace injection to exploit. Front-runner benefits most, but Mwafaq tracking in second and any horse that can organically sit prominent without over-racing is the primary winning profile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is controlled enough that a horse sitting second or third travels easily throughout and quickens clear turning for home with a well-timed challenge.
scenarios.body: Mwafaq, who has won twice on Good going at this trip range and wears a hood to keep focus, is ideally positioned to track the leader and produce a straightforward sustained challenge in the closing stages. His recent form — three wins in the last five — and consistent good-going record make him the standout profile for this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Reel In Tired Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Sanafi Zabeel, having led throughout on a longer than expected run, ties up inside the final furlong and leaves a gap for a horse with a strong finishing kick.
scenarios.body: Rajapour, who won last time over this course and distance on Good and was placed four times on similar going, has the profile to pick up late ground; Intrusively has also consistently placed on Good turf and could benefit from a final-furlong meltdown. This scenario requires the pace to be deceptively strong enough to bleed Sanafi Zabeel — not guaranteed given the lack of rivals pushing him.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos From Overcrowded Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the bunched midfield group results in shuffling and interference early, forcing several horses to race keenly or wide and creating an unpredictable finish.
scenarios.body: With nine horses all naturally wanting to sit midfield or behind, traffic problems and interference are plausible, potentially gifting a horse that finds a clean passage late an unexpected clear run. Starliner has placed twice on Good going over this trip and could benefit from any clearance, while Ephron's win on Good at a mile gives him a fighting chance if he threads through cleanly.

watchPoints.text: Mwafaq's early positioning is the single most important tactical moment — if Ethan Tindall (5) gets him to sit directly behind Sanafi Zabeel in second or third without burning fuel, he is ideally placed to deliver the race's most likely meaningful challenge.

Sanafi Zabeel's fractions in the opening half-mile will define the entire race shape — watch whether Paul Mulrennan bowls along unchallenged or, unusually, finds a rival willing to go with him, as any increase in pace changes every probability materially.

The compressed midfield group of Rajapour, Intrusively, Midsummer Storm, Starliner, Ephron, and Yaaser all seeking early positions creates a significant risk of crowding and interference from the gates — any horse drawn wide or slow away could be shuffled so far back that the moderate pace renders late ground-making impossible.

Watcha Snoop's confirmed tendency to fade in the finish, combined with being pushed into a midfield map position against her natural hold-up instinct, makes her a horse to watch early for signs of keenness or erratic behaviour that could unsettle those immediately around her.

Starliner's recent Good-going placed form at 8f (two 2nds from last three on Good) is quietly relevant given the going report confirms consistent Good conditions throughout the card — if the redistribution forces her to race closer than natural, her proven turf form could see her outrun her lower odds.

races.name: Wellman Cars Hamilton Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Braes Of Doune
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with solid recent form in similar Good-ground contests at this trip, placed twice in the last five runs at 8f on Good; sits ideally behind the lone front-runner and Paul Mulrennan is a course specialist — the visor is in place and 1d since last run is very short, worth monitoring for fitness freshness.
runners_data.comment: Braes Of Doune showed a second five starts back and has run over today's trip and going, with our rating of 57 ranking him second of nine — a genuine threat, though winless in his last five starts and the trainer's 5% strike rate over the past fortnight is a concern.

runners_data.name: Pisanello
runners_data.note: Recent dual winner over 8-9f on Good ground and a confirmed front-runner who gets to dictate here with zero pressure; Conor Whiteley (5lb claim) is an interesting booking for David O'Meara, and visors are retained — the 3d turnaround is tight but connections are clearly confident; the STYLE_FIT flag reflects that he wins from the front, which is exactly his role here.
runners_data.comment: Pisanello arrives in cracking form, back-to-back wins his calling card, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions. Carrying 138 lb from stall one, the top-rated runner here on a speed rating of 73, only the quick three-day turnaround gives any pause.

runners_data.name: Hostelry
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's veteran hold-up type has been a model of consistency, placing in four of his last five at 8f on Good, and steps up slightly in trip to 9f which should suit his staying style; Tom Eaves takes the ride after a 21-day break, and with no headgear flag this is a straightforward runner that simply needs a strong enough gallop to finish through — which this race shape may not provide.
runners_data.comment: Hostelry has run over today's trip and going before and, carrying 135 lb from stall 8, her rating of 57 gives her a solid claims here; the risk is she has been winless in her last six starts, with a string of fourth and fifth-place finishes suggesting a win may prove elusive.

runners_data.name: Defence Missile
runners_data.note: Won on Flat at 8f on Standard recently and returned from that break with a run at 8f on Good last week; a 4-year-old whose true style is hold-up, he steps up from sprint distances and the step to 1m1f may stretch him — Kaiya Fraser rides and trainer Linda Perratt has been in strong form (4/9 T14), making this one to respect despite the trip query.
runners_data.comment: Defence Missile won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, yet that victory followed four modest efforts, and carrying 134 lb from stall 2 tests whether he can back it up consistently.

runners_data.name: Jenson Benson
runners_data.note: Returned from a 291-day absence last time and ran 5th over 12f on Standard, so fitness is the primary question; his natural hold-up style over longer distances is genuine, but at 1m1f he will need to race closer than usual — mapped to midfield as the field is congested at the rear, but he is unlikely to get that position naturally, tempering his chance.
runners_data.comment: Jenson Benson has run over today's trip and going, and a second five starts back hints at ability worth respecting — our rating of 57 puts him notably above his official mark. The concern is 291 days off the track; that layoff is the obvious risk for a gelding yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Evelyn's Phoenix
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 5-year-old has form at this trip and won over 10f on Good, but a 48-day layoff and a run of moderate finishes (17th, 9th, 6th, 9th) since that win are concerning; tongue-tie and cheekpieces are retained, and while he is a true hold-up horse, the crowded rear of this field means he is pushed into midfield on the map — his chance hinges on a truly run race that this shape is unlikely to deliver.
runners_data.comment: Evelyn's Phoenix showed a second and a win in his last six starts but has since dipped into unplaced territory, and 48 days off raises fitness queries; he has distance and going experience to call on, though his official mark of 50 sets the ceiling.

runners_data.name: Can I Kiss You
runners_data.note: The finishing-fade flag is a significant concern for this 4-year-old who has finished 8th in three of his last five starts at 8f on Good; placed once at 8f on Good but that form is difficult to build on, and as a genuine hold-up horse operating in a congested rear he is mapped to midfield against his natural instincts — Andrew Mullen rides but the profile is uninspiring.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts with three eighths among them, Can I Kiss You faces a stiff task here — though she has run over today's trip and going before, and a second four starts back offers a scrap of encouragement; 130 lb from stall five won't help.

runners_data.name: Ring Of Gold
runners_data.note: Veteran of 9 years with no wins or places at all in his last five outings at distances from 7f to 8f on varied ground; Lewis Chalkley's 7lb claim offers some weight relief but the visor has not unlocked improvement and the sim-going strike rate (3/15) is the worst in the field — a true hold-up horse who will need everything to go right in a sprint finish.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a pair of sevenths in his two most recent outings, Ring Of Gold heads into this ranked bottom on our figures and faces a stiff ask; the experience over today's trip and going at least means he is not wholly in the dark.

runners_data.name: Saxon Grace
runners_data.note: The only 3-year-old in the race, dropped back from a 7f effort and attempting 9f for the first time, with all form at 5-7f on Good and Soft; Shane Gray rides for the lightly-raced Daragh Bourke yard (0/1 T14) and the step up in trip plus lack of course form makes this a significant unknown — natural hold-up style but no evidence of stamina for this distance.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Saxon Grace has struggled for consistency and ranks seventh of nine on our figures, making her hard to fancy here; she has run over today's going before and comes into this 26 days fresh, but there is little in her recent form to inspire confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Pisanello is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, is set to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop over the 1m1f trip on Good ground at Hamilton. Braes Of Doune is the only other horse with prominent tendencies and will likely slot in just behind, but there is nothing to force Pisanello into a contested early pace. The bulk of the field — Hostelry, Defence Missile, Jenson Benson, Evelyn's Phoenix, Can I Kiss You, Ring Of Gold, and Saxon Grace — are hold-up types, meaning the pace is likely to be steady to moderate and the race will not be truly run until well into the straight. This shape strongly favours horses that can travel close to a moderate gallop and produce a sustained finishing effort rather than deep closers who need genuine pace to close onto; prominent racers and hold-up types with strong finishing form at this trip will be best positioned. Note that the field holds more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear: Jenson Benson, Evelyn's Phoenix, Can I Kiss You, and Ring Of Gold are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, but in reality they will likely crowd the rear and struggle to find clear runs if the pace is modest.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pisanello Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Pisanello is allowed to bowl along unchallenged at a comfortable gallop and the hold-up brigade are left with too much to do from the rear.
scenarios.body: Pisanello dictates every yard from the front, setting a pace entirely on his own terms, and with a sustained run from the top of the straight he has every chance to win from the front on Good ground where he has recent winning form; Braes Of Doune, tracking closely, is ideally placed to pick up any scraps if Pisanello ties up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Outpace Prediction
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves quicker than expected and several hold-up horses get closer to Pisanello, setting up a stronger gallop that rewards late finishers.
scenarios.body: A genuinely run race allows the hold-up horses to travel with more momentum and pick off a tiring leader in the final furlong; Defence Missile, who returned to winning form recently, and Hostelry, consistent at this trip, are best equipped to finish through.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Sweeper Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the modest pace collapses into a sprint finish and one horse produces a decisive burst from just off the pace in the straight.
scenarios.body: Evelyn's Phoenix or Jenson Benson, if able to get a prominent enough position despite their true hold-up style, could benefit from a rush to the line in a muddling finish; however, both carry a style-fit discount having been redistributed from their natural rear position, making this outcome markedly less likely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Outsider Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the race becomes extremely tactical and the field bunches, allowing a hold-up horse at long odds to thread through in the straight.
scenarios.body: Ring Of Gold or Saxon Grace, racing off modest weights and sitting quietly at the rear, might find daylight in a blanket finish, though neither has the recent form or course figures to inspire confidence; this scenario is the least probable given the lack of strong pace to close onto.

watchPoints.text: Pisanello's pace — if Conor Whiteley (5lb claim) bowls along unchallenged and sets a comfortable gallop, the hold-up brigade at the rear may simply have too much ground to make up on Good ground.
Braes Of Doune's freshness — only 1 day since last run is an unusually short turnaround for an 8-year-old; monitor market moves and watch for any signs of physical readiness at the start.

Rear-field congestion — Jenson Benson, Evelyn's Phoenix, Can I Kiss You, and Ring Of Gold will all want to race from the back, creating potential for covering moves and blocked runs in the straight; any horse needing a clear passage from the rear faces a significant risk.

Defence Missile's trip stamina — he has won over 8f on Standard but this is his first attempt at 1m1f on Turf Good; if he fails to see out the trip he could stop quickly in the final furlong, affecting the finishing order behind him.

Ring Of Gold's course record — sim-going strike rate of just 3/15 on Good ground with zero wins or places at the course in recent runs; include in any late-price considerations only if the race completely falls apart for the principles.
